name: Does Denver's dry climate affect kitchen countertop installation and cabinetry?

mainEntity.name: Does Denver's dry climate affect kitchen countertop installation and cabinetry?

acceptedAnswer.text: In the Denver metro area, seasonal shifts between dry winter indoor heating and summer humidity cause natural wood framing and subfloors to expand and contract. This movement can pull base cabinets slightly out of level over time. Heavy stone slabs like granite or quartz require a perfectly flat surface; unlevel cabinets can cause seams to separate or stone to crack under load. As an Aurora-based finish contractor, Abraham Becerra inspects and levels cabinet runs specifically to account for local home movement before slabs are placed.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes. Climate shifts cause wood cabinets and framing to expand and contract. Proper leveling and shimming before setting heavy stone prevents seam separation and slab stress.
